title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a small category, (Ens) is the category of sets, A^ = Hom(A°,Ens) is presheaves on A, and A^∨ = Hom(A,Ens) is copresheaves. The isomorphisms only work with this variance for A^∨; A^{∨°} is its opposite.

(1) Top diagram, inside the big functor category Hom(A^∨,(Ens)):
- A^ ≃ Hom_!(A^∨,Ens). Hom_! means colimit-preserving functors. Since A^∨ = (A°)^ is the free cocompletion of A°, colimit-preserving functors A^∨→Ens are the same as functors A°→Ens. Concretely, F ∈ A^ goes to the coend G ↦ F⊗_A G.
- A^{∨°} ≃ Hom_rep(A^∨,Ens). By Yoneda, G ↦ Hom(G,−) identifies A^{∨°} with the corepresentable functors.
- Both are full subcategories of Hom(A^∨,(Ens)). Their intersection consists of the functors Hom(G,−) that commute with colimits, i.e. the tiny (small-projective) objects G of the presheaf category A^∨ = (A°)^. These are exactly the retracts of representables, Kar(A°). Grothendieck records this as (Kar(A°))° ≃ Kar(A), with A ⊂ Kar(A) (vertical arrow in the middle).
- Hence the right-hand diagram A = A^ ∩ A^{∨°} inside Σ(A): Σ(A) is the abstract category obtained as the union of A^ and A^{∨°} glued along A. It maps fully faithfully ('pl. fid.') to Hom(A^∨,(Ens)). Σ̄(A) is presumably the full image, i.e. the union of the two images.
- Hom-sets in this amalgam: from G (corepresentable) to F, Yoneda gives F⊗_A G. From F to Hom(G,−) one gets maps from F to a conjugate of G. So Σ(A) is a 'two-sided' envelope holding presheaves and opposites of copresheaves simultaneously, in the spirit of Isbell's envelope. This is the setting for a duality of topoi / 'correspondences' between A and A°, used on the next page (sheaves vs cosheaves, F(X,M)° ≃ F̌(X,M°)).

(2) Bottom: a general gluing lemma that abstracts the construction.
- Data: a category M with full subcategories M1, M2 and N = M1 ∩ M2. Categories M1', M2' with fully faithful functors M_i' → M_i, sharing a common full subcategory N' over N.
- Construction: Σ' = M1' ∪_{N'} M2'. Objects are the disjoint union glued along N'; Hom-sets are taken from M. There is a fully faithful functor Σ'→M factoring through M1 ∪ M2.
- Caveat: even if M1, M2 are strictly full (replete) in M, hence N strictly full, and the M_i' → M_i are equivalences, M_i' need not be strictly full in Σ', and N' → N need not be an equivalence. An object of M1' may be isomorphic in M to an object of M2' without lying in N'. The construction is a strict, not homotopy-invariant, pushout of categories.
- This is exactly the situation of Σ(A): A^ and A^{∨°} are glued along A, while their true intersection in Hom(A^∨,Ens) is Kar(A). So N' = A → N = Kar(A) fails to be an equivalence unless A is Karoubian. This explains why Σ(A) and Σ̄(A) differ.
errors: 'A = A^ ∩ A^{∨°}' holds only up to Karoubi envelope: the intersection in Hom(A^∨,Ens) is Kar(A). Grothendieck himself records this in the upper diagram, and the closing caveat is precisely about this discrepancy.
The isomorphism A^ ≃ Hom_!(A^∨,Ens) requires A^∨ = Hom(A,Ens) (not its opposite). The notation is consistent with that reading.

ideas.what: Presheaves on A ≃ colimit-preserving functors from copresheaves to Set (via the coend/tensor F⊗_A G)
ideas.modern_name: universal property of the free cocompletion / Eilenberg–Watts type
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. I (extension of functors to presheaf categories)

ideas.what: The intersection of presheaves and opposite copresheaves inside Hom(A^∨,Ens) is Kar(A): tiny objects of a presheaf category are the retracts of representables
ideas.where_published: Karoubi envelope appears in SGA4 Exp. I exercises (unsure about the tiny-object statement)

ideas.what: Category Σ(A) containing both A^ and A^{∨°} as full subcategories meeting in A, embedded fully faithfully in Hom(A^∨,Ens)
ideas.modern_name: Isbell envelope / collage of the Isbell conjugacy profunctor; related to the reflexive completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Isbell (1960s); Garner (2015, Isbell monad); Avery–Leinster (2021, reflexive completion)

ideas.what: Gluing of two categories along a common full subcategory via fully faithful maps into an ambient M; the strict union is not invariant under equivalence
ideas.modern_name: strict vs. pseudo/homotopy pushout of categories along fully faithful functors

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, for the purpose of topos duality and sheaf/cosheaf duality, a common envelope of presheaves and opposite copresheaves, i.e. an Isbell-envelope-type object. He realizes it inside Hom(A^∨,Ens) and identifies the intersection with Kar(A). This is a variant of the later Isbell envelope / reflexive completion line (Garner, Avery–Leinster), which does not cite or connect to Grothendieck's topos-duality motivation.
missed.quote: A = A^∩A^{∨°} ... (Kar(A°))° ≈ Kar(A) ... Σ(A) → Hom(A^∨,(Ens)) pl. fid.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows an independent appearance of the Isbell-envelope idea tied to sheaf/cosheaf duality (next page), but the mathematics itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard category theory: free cocompletion, the Karoubi envelope as tiny objects, and an Isbell-type amalgam. It is mildly interesting as an independent Grothendieck appearance of an Isbell-envelope construction in a topos-duality context, but nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The '7' at top left is a sheet number; '13' at bottom is the page number.
's.-cat [?] pleines pl. fid.' is better read as 'des sous-catégories pleines', with the side labels 'pl. fid.' on the vertical arrows M_i' → M_i.
The left diagram shows M_1' → M_1 and M_2' → M_2 (fully faithful) and N' → N, with N = M_1 ∩ M_2 and N' at the bottom.
The final clause reads roughly 'et N' → N n'est pas non plus une équivalence.'
In the upper diagram, Hom_rep(A^∨,(Ens)) is the corepresentable functors. The vertical chain is A → Kar(A) (A ↪ Kar).
